context:
Goal: a note stays while it is still being met, and expires when nobody meets it.
Problem (goal): PR #2785 (a note's sightings carry a date, and an old note expires) bumps Seen only on a repeat sighting. A note edited today keeps its old Seen date, so it can expire soon after someone worked on it.
Based on (ruling): owner item 358, the sightings ruling, which the PR adds to CLAUDE.md.
Departs from: main — adds a Seen date and an expiry window to notes; this question sets whether an edit refreshes Seen.
Meanwhile: corrected 11:40 CST Nov 12: #2785 (the pull request that adds Seen dates and expiry to notes) was closed at 10:26 CST, because it clashed with other record-check pull requests still in flight. Its branch is kept and reopens once those land. Your answer applies at that reopen; option b means the branch as built.

lastAnswer.note: who argued for option A? it does not sound better so trying to understand if i am naive or not

options.gain: A note someone just edited never expires right after.
options.how: The record-slug check and the sweep treat any change to a note's line as a sighting and set Seen to that day.
options.label: An edit refreshes Seen
options.lose: A cleanup edit (a reword, a moved path) keeps a dead note alive for another window.

options.gain: A note lives only while someone meets its problem again, so dead notes expire.
options.how: Keep the rule as the notes pull request built it: only a new sighting of the problem sets Seen.
options.label: Only a repeat sighting refreshes Seen (Recommended)
options.lose: A note edited today can expire soon after, unless someone records a new sighting.

reply: Triage marked a as recommended when it wrote this item; no one else argued for it. Your doubt is right: most edits are cleanups (a reword, a moved path), not a new meeting with the problem, so a would keep dead notes alive. Triage took b at 12:05 CST, since your note points there: only a repeat sighting refreshes Seen, as the notes pull request built it. To change it, answer again here.
short: Notes: does an edit refresh Seen
title: When someone edits a note that carries a Seen date, does the edit count as a new sighting?
why: Recommended: b. Most edits are cleanups, not a new meeting with the problem, so refreshing Seen on an edit would keep dead notes alive.
